# AgentAuth Protocol v0.2

Canonical source:
https://github.com/imMamdouhaboammar/agent-auth-protocol

Original system design:
Mamdouh Aboammar

Status:
Draft system design. AgentAuth is not an Internet standard and is not yet a production-ready reference implementation.

## One-sentence definition

AgentAuth is an open protocol and system-design profile for AI agent identity, authentication, authorization, delegation, federation, runtime attestation, and native Login as Agent.

## Problem

Existing identity systems can authenticate humans, OAuth clients, service accounts, and workloads, but they do not automatically preserve all AI-agent security semantics at once.

AgentAuth makes these identities explicit:

- Agent Principal: durable AI-agent security principal
- Agent Instance: one running instance with its own proof key
- Subject: human, organization, workload, or Agent represented by the Actor
- Delegation Grant: scoped authority permitting the Agent to act
- Provider Agent Account: Provider-local mapping to an issuer-qualified Agent Principal
- AgentAuth Context: immutable Provider-side context created after validation
- Agent Session: Provider session that remains server-side distinguishable from a human session

The canonical global Agent Principal identity is the pair (agent_issuer, agent_id).

## Three-party architecture

Agent Client / Agent SDK
  -> AgentAuth Authority
  -> Provider / Provider SDK

The Authority may be operated by the Provider, Agent owner, enterprise identity team, cloud platform, or independent identity provider.

AgentAuth does not require one global root.

## Login as Agent

Native Login as Agent means the target intentionally accepts an AI Agent Actor.

It is not ordinary browser automation.

A Provider can preserve:

Subject
Agent Principal
Agent Instance
Delegation Grant
Proof method
Protocol version
Provider-local session state

A native browser session remains marked actor_type=ai_agent on the server.

## Authorization

Effective authority is an intersection.

Delegated mode:

Requested Authority
INTERSECT Subject Authority
INTERSECT Delegation Grant
INTERSECT Agent Local Authority
INTERSECT Provider Policy Allow
INTERSECT Runtime Authority
MINUS Provider Policy Deny

One broad permission source cannot restore authority narrowed by another layer.

Portable grants use positive Capabilities.

Unknown authority-bearing constraints fail closed.

Child delegation can only attenuate actions, Resources, constraints, lifetime, and delegation depth.

## Consent and approval

AgentAuth separates a structured Authorization Proposal from the raw natural-language prompt.

Progressive consent allows optional Capabilities to be omitted or narrowed.

Sensitive transaction approval can bind to an Action Digest.

The Action Digest is derived from a canonical structured Action Intent, not a raw prompt.

Approval Evidence satisfies an obligation but does not expand an existing grant.

## Trust and federation

Cryptographically valid does not equal locally trusted.

Trusted issuer does not equal trusted runtime.

Trusted runtime does not equal authorized action.

Federation is explicit, directional, bounded, revocable, and non-transitive by default.

A Provider can directly trust a foreign Home Authority or use a Provider Authority to broker/exchange foreign credentials into local credentials.

Brokered exchange can change the access-token issuer while preserving canonical agent_issuer and Agent identity provenance.

## Runtime attestation

Runtime Attestation is a trust input, not a permission grant.

AgentAuth aligns with the RATS architecture and can use EAT-based attestation profiles.

Attestation may describe workload, software, hardware, measured components, proof-key binding, and freshness.

Provider policy decides whether specific assurance evidence is required for an Action.

AgentAuth does not define a universal numeric assurance ladder.

## SPIFFE

SPIFFE identifies workloads.

AgentAuth identifies AI Agent Principals and Agent Instances.

A valid SPIFFE workload identity requires an explicit trusted mapping to an Agent Principal.

SPIFFE trust does not automatically grant AgentAuth federation or Provider permission.

## Standards posture

AgentAuth is standards-first.

Stable foundations include OAuth 2.0, OAuth security best current practice, OAuth Token Exchange, DPoP, mTLS, Rich Authorization Requests, JWT access-token profiles, OAuth Resource Indicators, OAuth Authorization Server Metadata, OAuth Protected Resource Metadata, OpenID Connect, RATS, EAT, and SPIFFE concepts.

Emerging AI-agent identity and workload-identity drafts are research inputs until stable.

## Machine-readable contracts

The schemas directory contains JSON Schema contracts for AgentAuth claims, metadata, capabilities, constraints, grants, AgentAuth Context, trust decisions, attestation results, federation peers, enrollment, and related artifacts.

## Search-oriented terminology

AgentAuth addresses:

AI agent authentication
AI agent identity
AI agent authorization
agentic authentication
agent authorization protocol
Login as Agent
AI agent OAuth
AI agent access control
AI agent delegation
agent-to-agent delegation
non-human identity
machine identity for AI agents
MCP authentication
MCP authorization
AI agent federation
AI agent attestation
AI agent security protocol

These phrases describe the actual project scope and are not independent products or aliases.
